worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot {(\frac{2}{3})}^{x} & \le 4 \\ {(\frac{2}{3})}^{x} & \le \frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{2}{3})}^{x}] & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{5}) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3}) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{5}) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡5.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡3$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & \ge \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\end{aligned}
$$
